title: IPO (maximise capital)
pattern: unlock by threshold, pick by heap
statement: You start with capital w and may complete at most k projects. Project i needs capital[i] to start and adds profits[i] to your capital when done (capital is not consumed). Return the maximum final capital.
hints: Among affordable projects, the most profitable is always the right choice (it only increases what you can afford later).
Sort by capital; push newly affordable projects into a max-heap of profits.
complexity: O(n log n + k log n)

solution.explanation: A greedy with two moving parts: a pointer over projects sorted by capital ("what's affordable now") and a max-heap of affordable profits ("what's best now"). Exchange argument: swapping any chosen project for the most profitable affordable one never reduces capital at any later step. The pattern, unlock candidates by a threshold, choose among them by a heap, recurs in scheduling problems (course schedule III, minimum refuelling stops).
solution.python:
import heapq

import heapq

def find_maximized_capital(k, w, profits, capital):
    proj = sorted(zip(capital, profits))
    h = []
    i = 0
    for _ in range(k):
        while i < len(proj) and proj[i][0] <= w:
            heapq.heappush(h, -proj[i][1])
            i += 1
        if not h:
            break
        w -= heapq.heappop(h)
    return w
